text:
Claude initially mistook a car-insurance claim for a skiing accident. The fix was to give it the context it was missing.

Anthropic’s Prompting 101 walks through a Swedish accident form and a handwritten sketch. The useful lessons:

• Explain the form and messy human markings.
• Read the form first, then cross-check the sketch.
• Ask it to flag unclear evidence instead of guessing.
• Define the output your application actually needs.

It’s a 2025 session, so check model-specific advice: newer Claude models no longer support assistant-response prefill.

If you’re building document workflows, this is a useful reminder: turn the judgment you take for granted into clear instructions, then test them on difficult cases.
editorial_notes: Official session presented May 22 2025, published July 31 2025.
The X intermediary splits the recording into 16:00, 5:01 and 3:48 segments; it inaccurately describes Claude Code features.
Official transcript confirms form context, messy annotations, analysis order, grounded uncertainty and output formatting. Form-first is scenario-specific, not a universal multimodal rule.
The official transcript suggests using extended thinking to improve prompts but provides no 80 percent saving guarantee.
Current official docs say prefills are unsupported starting Claude 4.6; use structured outputs or explicit formatting instructions.
Selected video is the full official publication, acquired freshly for this task. Partial intermediary downloads are not accepted assets.
